system.text:
You plan one single-file HTML5 mini-game from a short brief.

Read the brief, then decide:

- `gameType`: one of `arcade-run`, `stage-clear`, `puzzle-board`, `toy-box`. Call `list_cards` with kind `type` and read the card that fits before you choose. Pick `toy-box` when the brief has no way to lose.
- `input`: one of `tap-anywhere`, `drag-follow`, `swipe-lanes`. Prefer `tap-anywhere` unless the brief asks for dragging or lanes.
- `style`: one of `paper-cut`, `chalkboard`, `risograph`.
- `title`: a short, playable name in the brief's language, at most 48 characters.
- `slug`: the title in lowercase ASCII words joined by single hyphens.
- `lang`: `en` or `fr`, the language the brief is written in.
- `loop`: one or two sentences, at most 280 characters, saying what the player does, what they are trying to reach and what ends a play-through.

Keep the game small enough to fit in one page with no external files. When the brief asks for something the contract forbids (sound files, network calls, saved progress), plan the closest version that fits and say nothing about the rest.

Answer only with the structured plan.

content.text:
Brief:

A long brief for a canal boat game. The player steers a narrow wooden boat along a city canal at dusk, and the view scrolls upward so the canal keeps coming toward the boat. The boat sits in one of three channels, and the player drags a finger left or right to move it between them. Moored barges, low bridges and floating crates block the channels, and they arrive faster as the run goes on. Lanterns float between the obstacles; each lantern collected adds to the score, and a lantern that is missed simply drifts away. There is only one boat, so the first collision ends the run. Please make the water a deep teal, the barges a warm brown and the lanterns a soft orange, with thin white lines for the ripples. I would also like a gentle splash sound whenever a lantern is collected and a low horn when the boat hits something, if that is possible. During play, show the score in the top corner in a clear, readable font. At the end, show how many lanterns were collected, say what the boat hit, and offer a way to set off again. The first few seconds should be calm, with no obstacles at all, so a new player can learn to steer before anything arrives.
